problem: Existing query/TrackID descriptors average three sparse observations and cannot reveal their internal appearance variation.
hypothesis: Per-anchor descriptors can expose variation hidden by the mean; this is a representation audit, not a claim of identity switches or improved RMOT.
intervention: Retain the identical three source row indices, compute the existing three-part HSV histograms per anchor, and exactly reconstruct both source-pair means.
controls: First/last and adjacent anchors within a provided ID; deterministic same-frame cyclic neighboring different provided IDs. No control is verified by target GT.

fixed_design.descriptor: Existing 104-dimensional normalized HSV histogram per part

inputs: Target images, fixed candidate rows and existing image-only mean descriptors; no image QA, prediction, target GT or source model forward.
fairness: All future ordinary and structured KD methods must receive identical per-anchor inputs.
boundaries: Three anchors cannot detect all interior changes. Color variation does not establish semantic errors, physical ID purity or a gain from temporal memory.
costs: Record image decoding, histogram processing and controller wall. This is shared preparation, not a complete cold method cost.
